title: Facilities Architect
description: About Focused Energy Focused Energy is building the future of clean energy through laser-driven inertial fusion. Backed by our $240M Series A — the largest fully secured Series A in the global fusion industry — we are scaling rapidly across multiple geographies. Based in Germany and the US, we have brought together the top scientific and engineering minds using proven technologies to unlock fusion power at commercial scale. Focused Energy is working to realize game-changing scientific innovation that promises to deliver a clean, sustainable and abundant source of power globally. Your Role Focused Energy is developing its flagship fusion facility at Biblis, Germany — and this role sits at the heart of making it happen. As Facility Development Lead, you will be the senior bridge between our engineering teams, the RWE/Biblis site stakeholders, German design and permitting requirements, utilities providers, and external planning partners. Without this role, Biblis development would slow down, RWE discussions would be less focused, and facility requirements could become fragmented. Engineering leaders would carry too much of the facility strategy and stakeholder interface burden. You will remove that risk by owning the facility development direction end-to-end. Your primary mission: turn Focused Energy’s technical and strategic needs for Biblis into a clear, realistic, and executable facility development plan — and keep it moving. What You'll Do Define the Biblis facility development direction by translating FE’s technical requirements into a phased, executable site, building, and infrastructure plan. • Lead the RWE and site-owner interface on facility planning, infrastructure constraints, utilities, and long-term site expansion, collaborating closely with the Senior Construction Project Manager. • Translate engineering’s needs into facility requirements across lasers, targetry, diagnostics, controls, cleanrooms, electrical systems, safety and operations. • Drive German design and permitting strategy by identifying required approvals, regulatory constraints, fire protection requirements, and risk assessment. • Coordinate external architects, planners, consultants and utilities partners, ensuring their output is aligned with FE’s technical roadmap and decision needs. • Enable senior decision-making by maintaining a clear, current picture of facility options, risks, assumptions, dependencies, and cost/schedule implications, so engineering leadership can act with confidence and without delay. Who You Are Must-haves Experience leading or shaping complex facility, industrial building, infrastructure, or technical site development in Germany. Working knowledge of German building, planning, permitting, and compliance processes. Ability to translate technical engineering needs into facility, layout, infrastructure, and utility requirements. Ability to manage external architects, planners, consultants, or engineering service providers. Strong stakeholder interface experience with site owners, authorities, landlords, utilities, or senior external partners. Professional German and English language capability. Nice-to-haves Experience with energy, nuclear-adjacent, research, cleanroom, laser, laboratory, or high-tech industrial facilities. Direct experience with RWE, grid operators, utilities providers, or major German site owners. Experience with phased campus or brownfield site development. Familiarity with power infrastructure, backup power, grid connection, HVAC, cooling, cleanrooms, or specialist utilities. Architectural, civil, building services, industrial engineering, or related professional qualification. Experience supporting investment cases, board-level decision papers, or strategic facility roadmaps. Focused Energy is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Focused Energy will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, benefits.

title: (Senior) Software Engineer (d/f/m)
description: Our story: Every year millions of people are either filing their taxes in fear or giving up on their tax refund altogether. We're working on fixing that. Our intuitive app enables anyone, regardless of education or background, to file their taxes with newfound confidence. Spread across Germany, Spain and the UK, the team at Taxfix Group with its brands Taxfix and Steuerbot, is a compassionate group of solution-finders. We speak our minds openly, and with over 400 professionals, including tax experts, developers, and IT security experts, we're rich in ideas and voices. The group has facilitated more than 3.5 billion euros in tax refunds for its customers since its founding in 2016. The opportunity : As a (Senior) Software Engineer, you’ll build core features for our flagship product, turning complex tax scenarios into simple, reliable experiences. You’ll bring a builder-first mindset: staying close to customer problems, using AI and modern engineering tools to move from idea to impact quickly, and taking ownership of outcomes—not just code. You’ll work hands-on in a cross-functional team and bring deep expertise in either frontend or backend engineering, while collaborating effectively across the stack. You’ll help us raise the bar for scalable design, quality, maintainability, and AI-first software development. Your responsibilities and decisions: Partner with product management, design, and engineering to understand customer problems, shape pragmatic solutions, and deliver measurable outcomes. Own work end to end—from discovery and technical design through implementation, release, monitoring, and iteration. Turn ambiguity into action, make sound trade-offs, and deliver valuable increments without compromising long-term maintainability. Contribute to technical direction and strategy in support of the long-term product vision. Use AI-assisted development tools in your daily engineering work to accelerate exploration, implementation, testing, debugging, and documentation while maintaining high engineering standards. Critically evaluate, validate, and troubleshoot AI-generated output, using effective prompting and appropriate safeguards rather than accepting results at face value. Share effective AI-assisted development practices, encourage responsible experimentation, and help teammates improve how they use AI tools. Improve developer experience through tools, automation, and engineering practices that enable reliable, frequent delivery. Collaborate across product and platform teams, and contribute to an environment where people learn, grow, give constructive feedback, and raise challenges safely. Your profile: Professional software engineering experience (React, Node.js) and designing reliable backend services and APIs. Experience with React Native experience is a plus. Able to work effectively across system boundaries and collaborate with engineers outside your primary specialism. Use AI-assisted development tools in your daily engineering work to accelerate exploration, implementation, testing, debugging, and documentation while maintaining high engineering standards. Able to evaluate and troubleshoot AI-generated output, use effective prompting where relevant, and share practical learnings with teammates. Experience working with a public cloud environment such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Microsoft Azure. Familiarity with DevOps concepts and practices, including CI/CD, observability, and operating software in production. Understanding of core application and backend concepts such as authentication, databases, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and API integrations. A builder-first, pragmatic approach: You turn customer problems into shipped outcomes. You take initiative, test and learn quickly, and make clear trade-offs between speed, quality, maintainability, and risk. Passion for writing maintainable, elegant code and continuously improving how software is built. A collaborative, positive attitude and a willingness to challenge ideas constructively. You have a builder mindset. You thrive in environments where things are still taking shape, take initiative to move ideas forward, and find ways to create impact even when the path isn't fully defined. You embrace trying things out over waiting for perfect conditions, ship early to learn fast, and treat iteration as progress. Why Taxfix? A chance to do meaningful, people-centric work with an international team of passionate professionals. Holistic well-being with free mental health coaching sessions and yoga. A monthly allowance to spend on an extensive range of services that you can use and roll over as flexibly as you like. Employee stock options for all employees—because everyone deserves to benefit from the success they help to create. 30 annual vacation days and flexible working hours. Work from abroad for up to six weeks every year. Just align with your team, and then enjoy your trip. Plenty of opportunities to socialise as a team. In addition to internal tech meetups, our international team hosts regular get-togethers—virtually and in person when possible. Free tax declaration filing, of course, through the Taxfix app—and internal support for all personal tax-related questions. Have a four-legged friend in your life? We’re happy to have dogs join us in the office. Excited? So are we. Check out our Life at Taxfix page on LinkedIn to get a glimpse of our culture. At Taxfix, we believe that incredible things happen when you have a wealth of perspectives and experiences. We're proudly committed to equal employment and development opportunities no matter your gender, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, colour, disability, or place of origin. To help mitigate any potential unconscious biases, we ask that you refrain from including your picture, age, or marital status on your CV. Let your experiences speak for themselves. Not sure if you meet all the requirements for this role? Please apply anyway. You might bring something special to the team that we hadn't considered previously.

title: Senior Information Security Manager (EU Sovereignty)

BSI C5 Maintain and mature our risk register, policy library, vendor/third-party risk assessments, and control monitoring Audits & evidence Act as a hands-on participant in audits, working directly with auditors, control owners, and leadership to prepare, execute, and close out certification and attestation cycles efficiently rather than through brute force Build and refine evidence collection processes using automation and GRC tooling (e.g. Vanta or similar), reducing manual overhead and audit fatigue across the company Design and roll out a model where product and engineering teams own their evidence throughout the control lifecycle, rather than compliance chasing people down before every audit Risk & business partnership Assess risk pragmatically: identify real security and compliance exposure, size it accurately, and make calculated calls that unblock product and engineering teams Partner with engineering, product, IT, People, and Legal to embed security and compliance requirements into existing workflows rather than bolting them on afterward Track regulatory and customer-driven compliance requirements — new customer security questionnaires, evolving frameworks — and translate them into practical, actionable controls Reporting Report on the state of the security and compliance program to stakeholders and leadership, including audit readiness, open risks, and remediation progress Qualities we look for 3-5 years of experience in information security, GRC, or compliance roles, ideally at a SaaS company, and ideally at scaleup pace and scale Hands-on experience running or supporting ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II programs and audits, from control design through evidence collection to certification Experience with HIPAA and/or BSI C5 is a strong plus Practical experience with GRC/evidence automation tooling such as Vanta (or equivalent), including building smooth, low-friction processes around it A track record of building processes that shift evidence ownership to the teams generating the evidence, rather than centralizing it all in compliance Sound risk judgment: comfortable making calculated, defensible risk decisions to keep product teams unblocked, rather than reflexively blocking Strong stakeholder management skills; able to work credibly with engineers, product managers, and leadership without becoming an obstacle Fluent English and German language skills at C1 level (or close by) are required Clear, structured communicator who can translate compliance requirements into language engineering and product teams actually act on What we offer Diverse and internationally distributed team : joining our team means becoming part of a large, global community with people of more than 90 nationalities. We're more than just colleagues; we're a group of professionals with a shared mission to connect diverse cultures. Our global presence is growing–we've doubled in size nearly every year, with our employees based in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, the US, and Japan, and we continue to expand our network. Open communication, regular feedback : as a language-focused company, we value the importance of clear, honest communication. We value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and growth mindset makes us better together. This allows you to engage directly with your team and experience the unique energy of our workspace, while still enjoying the flexibility and comfort of working from home. With flexible working hours and trust in your productivity, we are in sync with your team’s general locations and time zones to foster effective and seamless collaboration. Virtual Shares - An ownership mindset in every role. We believe everyone should share in our success, and that’s why every employee receives Virtual Shares, linking your contribution directly to DeepL’s growth and rewarding you with a stake in our future. Regular in-person team events : we bond over vibrant events that are as unique as our team, from local team and business unit gatherings, to new-joiner onboardings, to company-wide events that bring us all together–literally. Monthly full-day hacking sessions : every month, we have Hack Fridays, where you can spend your time diving into a project you're passionate about and get the opportunity to work with other teams–we value your initiatives, impact, and creativity. 30 days of annual leave : we value your peace of mind. Frontend craft — Deep expertise in modern frontend engineering, with strong command of TypeScript, component architecture, state management, design systems, accessibility, performance, testing, and maintainable application architecture. AI-native practice — You use AI coding tools daily and have gone past autocomplete into agentic workflows. You have a considered view on where they genuinely help, where they don't, and what a codebase needs to be a good place to work in with agents. Product judgment — You care about the user experience as much as the technical solution. You can translate ambiguous workflows and business constraints into pragmatic, elegant product experiences. Systems thinking — You are comfortable reasoning across frontend, backend, APIs, infrastructure, observability, security, and compliance when the problem requires it. Operating style — You think in quarters and years, not only sprints. You drive cross-team change through credibility, clear writing, architectural reasoning, and strong stakeholder alignment — not through authority. Collaborative Leadership: A proactive relationship-builder who can set technical direction and influence without formal authority, manage diverse stakeholders and build alignment on difficult technical decisions, while mentoring engineers. Language — Fluent English, written and spoken. You can make complex technical decisions legible to engineers, product partners, design partners, and leadership alike. Our tech stack Frontend: TypeScript, React, Svelte — we are consolidating on React, and this role leads that migration. Backend: TypeScript, Node.js, Nest.js Database: MySQL Infrastructure: Kubernetes on AWS Source Control & CI/CD: GitHub Authentication: FusionAuth, Okta Internal Tools: Retool Messaging: Twilio, SendGrid Forms: Tally Workplace & Benefits Customizable benefits package covering wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays Remote-flexible hybrid setup Up to 6 remote calendar weeks a year A great tech and work setup Work with a diverse team of 130+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains Hiring process Initial screening with Talent Acquisition (30 min): get acquainted with bunch, explore your motivation, and understand whether what we offer matches what you are looking for. Hiring Manager call — Engineering (60 min): a conversation with Engineering leadership focused on your scope, frontend leadership, product-engineering mindset, and how you diagnose and lead systemic improvements. Technical Interview (60 min): a hands-on technical conversation focused on frontend engineering craft, TypeScript, component design, maintainability, testing, and pragmatic problem-solving. Technical Interview — System Design (60 min): a frontend/system design conversation focused on architecture, data flow, performance, accessibility, reliability, and trade-offs in complex product systems. VP Product conversation (45 min): a cross-functional conversation focused on product thinking, customer empathy, business acumen, and how you partner with Product and Design on ambiguous problems. Final round (45 min): a closing conversation to align on what we heard across the process, answer remaining questions, and discuss expectations for the role and trial period. title: Head of Engineering (f/m/d)
description: At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions. Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next. We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process. This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both. How we're set up Tribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do. We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves. What you'll own Feasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible. The people. 15 to 20 direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, expectations, feedback, development, compensation and promotion recommendations, and the tough calls that keep talent density high. Tech Leads feed you performance signals; the decisions and the conversations are yours. Technical judgement across squads. Broad understanding of the tribe's systems and how they fit into the wider Moss architecture. You challenge estimates and technical proposals from your engineers; you don't produce the estimates yourself. A seat in the tribe trio. Roadmap and planning input through a feasibility lens. You argue solutions and trade-offs with the Product Tribe Lead as a technical peer, and push back on scope and timelines when the engineering picture says so. Operating rhythm. How the tribe plans, estimates, tracks and reports on delivery, with proactive, timely transparency to the tribe and to leadership, the good and the bad. Capacity. Putting your best people on the most impactful work, moving engineers between squads (and, where it serves Moss, between tribes) while still letting people build real domain depth. Alignment across tribes. Tribe leads aren't isolated trios. You align proactively with your peer Heads of Engineering and with platform and architecture owners, and you resolve shared-architecture questions through alignment, not around it. How we expect leaders to operate Velocity first, with high agency. Working smart and hard on the right problems. Lead by example, stay close to the work. You know the details of what your team is building and course-correct in real time. You get hands-on when speed or quality is on the line. End-to-end ownership of outcomes. Responsibility doesn't stop at your team's boundary. Make changes elsewhere when that's what it takes, communicating first, not unilaterally. No waterfall, no blame. Product, Design and Engineering work together from the start. If there's a gap in the trio, fill it or name it. Disagree and commit. Challenge when it matters. Once a call is made, own the message and explain the why, including for calls you argued against. Proactive expertise. We build expert products for finance teams. Decisions rest on real expertise, internal and external, not assumptions. Moss has one manager framework for every people leader, and this role is held to it in full: build a high-performing team, define success clearly, deliver results with your team, and operate with speed and ownership. You can hold us to it too. What you bring 4 to 6+ years in engineering management , with a track record of managing engineers directly at a meaningful span. You've run hiring, performance management and difficult conversations yourself, not through a layer of managers. A senior engineering career before that. You've operated at senior or staff level as an engineer and your judgement on system design is current, not historical. Strong systems design. You can read an architecture, spot where it will break, and argue an alternative with the people who built it. You can tell a 2-week estimate from a 6-week one and explain why. Comfort as a technical peer to product leadership. You've shaped roadmaps and scope through feasibility arguments, and you've won and lost those arguments gracefully. Structure at scale without a middle layer. You build the practices that make 15 to 20 direct reports work: clear expectations, regular feedback, visible delivery. Fast in unfamiliar domains. You can reason about a new technical domain quickly and contribute before you have deep prior expertise in it. Experience from an environment with mature engineering practices : code review, testing, incident handling, planning and estimation that actually work. You know what good looks like and can build it where it's missing. Strong pluses Background at an AI product company or in ERP / financial systems. Both are directly relevant to what we build. Experience leading in a flat or tribe/squad-style organisation. Experience with a Tech Lead / Engineering Manager split, as either side of it. What this role is, and isn't It's worth being clear about the shape of the job. Your technical contribution is judgement, challenge and architecture-level input; Tech Leads own the how and write the code alongside their squads, so this isn't a role with an IC workload attached. And it's a role where you manage engineers, not managers: every engineer in the tribe reports to you directly, there is no management layer beneath you, and we don't plan to add one. If that combination of deep people leadership and real technical engagement is what you're looking for, you'll find a lot to like here. About Moss Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work. Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. In August 2026, Moss closed a €35 million Series C led by Portage, crossing a €1 billion valuation and becoming one of Europe's newest fintech unicorns. Moss is backed by investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star. We're a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities across 5 offices in Europe and we hire, reward, and grow people based on Moss DNA : playing to win, obsessing over quality, winning as One Moss. If that's how you want to work, we want to hear from you. - here's what else to expect: Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos. Additional benefits include: 20 days “work from abroad”, 600EUR/GBP Learning & Development Budget, and other local benefits. Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package).
